propositions: A new locked dirty-tree commit and push entrypoint must stage and commit uncommitted tracker changes before delegating to the push-only primitive, preserving reconciler events and bridge-bot authorship.

The entrypoint must acquire and hold the tracker's write lock, verify no rebase/merge-recovery is in progress (strict mode raises PushDeliveryError with merge-recovery-blocked; default mode warns and returns), then stage and commit all dirty changes only when necessary.
Per-commit git identity must be applied via git -c flags without mutating global or repository config; supplied name/email takes precedence over ambient repository identity.

A clean but locally-ahead tracker must push without creating an empty commit; persistent rejection under strict mode preserves the local commit and raises PushDeliveryError; default mode retains uncommitted content for retry.

Strict lock, staging, or commit failures must raise the exact dependency-defined PushDeliveryError with stable named reasons; default mode logs a warning, returns without push, and retains content for later clean retry.
The existing push_tickets_branch function must remain push-only and never stage or commit a dirty tree; the new entrypoint is a separate internal composite operation.
